draft.title: Work and identity
card: Identity is how a person sees themselves and what they think makes them who they are. Work can be part of this. A person may say "I am a nurse" or "I am a farmer" when they describe themselves.
Work can also shape a person's role in the community. A teacher, a volunteer firefighter or a shop owner is often known and relied on by others for what they do.
Work affects standard of living, which is how well off a person or family is, such as the food, housing and services they can afford. Income from work can help pay for these things.
Work is not the only thing that shapes identity. Family, culture, interests and beliefs matter too, and people without paid work still have an identity and a role.
draft.remember: Work can shape how people see themselves, the role they play in the community, and how well they live.

a.q: Tom has been a bus driver in Hobart for 20 years. He says, "Driving is who I am." What does this show?
opts: His work has shaped how he sees himself
His work has set his standard of living
His work is the only part of his identity
His work is the same as his role in the community
a.why: Saying that driving is who he is shows work shaping his identity, which is how he sees himself. Standard of living is about what a person can afford, not how they describe themselves. The card also says work is not the only thing that shapes identity.
a.clue: Think about how he describes himself.

b.q: Priya volunteers as a surf lifesaver at a beach in Perth. Neighbours know her as the person who keeps the beach safe. Which idea does this best show?
opts: Work shaping a person's role in the community
Work raising a person's standard of living
Work being the only source of identity
Work being limited to paid jobs
b.why: Priya is known and relied on by others for what she does, so her work shapes her role in the community. Volunteering is unpaid, so it does not raise her standard of living through income. The example says nothing to suggest work is the only source of identity.
b.clue: Look at how other people see her.

a.best: His work has shaped how he sees himself

b.best: Work shaping a person's role in the community
